title: Twelve Stones Over His Heart
summary: Aaron the priest receives special clothes: a breastplate with twelve colorful stones, one for each tribe, and little bells that ring when he walks. Every evening he lights the menorah. A story about how each of us is a precious stone, and how someone carries us close to their heart.
pages:
Aaron was the High Priest.
Every day he worked in the Mishkan, God's house in the middle of the camp.

One day they brought Aaron new clothes.
A long blue robe, a white tunic, and a turban for his head.
Aaron turned around in front of everyone, and the clothes shone.

On his chest they placed a breastplate, and in the breastplate were twelve precious stones.
Red, green, blue, yellow, purple...
Like a little rainbow.

On each stone was carved the name of one tribe:
Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph and Benjamin.

"Why do you need so many stones?" asked a little boy.
Aaron smiled: "Because every tribe is important. And if even one stone is missing, the breastplate isn't whole."

And the breastplate sat right over Aaron's heart.
So every time he went into the Mishkan, he carried all the people of Israel on his heart.

On his shoulders, too, he had two stones, with the names of all the tribes on them.
It was as if Aaron were saying: "I carry all of you with me."

And along the hem of the blue robe hung little golden bells, with colorful pomegranates in between.
Ding, ding, ding!
When Aaron walked, everyone could hear him coming.

And every evening, when the sun went down, Aaron lit the menorah with pure olive oil.
The light burned all night long, until morning.

The children in the camp loved to look at the little light from far away.
"Aaron has already lit it," they told each other, and fell asleep peacefully.

You, too, and every boy and girl, are precious stones.
Each of you has your own color, your own light.
And without any one of you, the world isn't whole.
